text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- South Korea's industrial giant Daewoo Corp is expected to start negotiations this week on launching car production in Bulgaria, Foreign Investment Agency's director Daniela Bobeva said.
-- Bulgaria's Finance Ministry said the rehabilitation programme of the indebted national carrier Balkan Airlines is inefficient and demanded that a new one is worked out, company officials said.

-- Bulgarian National Bank (BNB)'s foreign currency reserves amounted to some $540 million at the end of August, up by $17 million from the month before due to net foreign currency purchases on the domestic forex market, BNB preliminary data shows.

--Some 12 privatisation funds will not be able to register for participation in Bulgaria's voucher privatisation programme because they have not raised the minimum capital required for a licence, Mass Privatisation Centre's executive director Kalin Mitrev said.
-- Direct foreign investment in Bulgaria fell 36 percent year-on-year to $49 million in the first half of 1996, Bulgarian National Bank's figures show.
-- Bulgaria's President Zhelyu Zhelev, a staunch anti-communist, slammed the Socialist cabinet of premier Zhan Videnov for bringing the country to economic collapse.
-- A two-day Balkan gas conference, organised by the Balkan and Black Sea Gas and Oil Association, starts in Sofia today.

-- Bulgaria's Euroenergy Holding, which bought 75 percent of the debt-ridden Plama oil refinery for 62 million levs, pledged to pay $111.7 million and seven billion levs of Plama's debts, a holding official said.

-- Indebted state firms earmarked for liquidation under Bulgaria's structural reform programme agreed with multilateral lenders will be closed by the end of September, Deputy Prime minister Roumen Gechev told the national television.
-- More than a thousand Jews from around the world gathered on Sunday to re-inaugurate Sofia synagogue, Bulgaria's biggest and one of the most ornate in Europe.
